extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, news startup founders, and readers interested in journalism innovation
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational 'About' page describing the Nieman Journalism Lab’s mission, staff, partnerships, licensing, and what kinds of journalism work and contributions the Lab seeks to highlight and encourage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial mission — help journalism adapt to the Internet age
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nieman Journalism Lab exists to help journalism figure out its future in an Internet age; it focuses on highlighting attempts at innovation and figuring out what makes them succeed or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit aims include: find good ideas for others to steal; help reporters and editors adjust to online work; help traditional news organizations find ways to survive; help new startups that will complement or supplant traditional organizations. Use coverage and analysis that surface lessons from experiments and innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection focus — spotlight attempts at innovation and assess outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab emphasizes highlighting attempts at innovation and analyzing why they succeed or fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should examine experiments (e.g., crowdsourcing, new business models, technology adoption) and draw actionable lessons. The page’s listed posts (crowdsourcing, reinvention of classifieds, R&D labs, archives, etc.) illustrate the topical focus and expected case-study style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader-contributed, collaborative exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary among the Lab’s resources are its readers; the Lab expects and encourages reader contributions to make the site a collaborative exchange of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are invited to tell the Lab what’s happening around them or what should be. Contributions from practitioners and readers are welcomed and seen as an important input to coverage and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Foundation programs and standards — fellowship information and institutional mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nieman Foundation at Harvard administers midcareer fellowships and other programs (Nieman Reports, Nieman Program on Narrative Journalism, Nieman Watchdog Journalism Project) that support study, critical examination, and watchdog journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical detail included: fellowship annual deadlines (December 15 for international journalists; January 31 for Americans). The Foundation’s stated goals include encouraging reporters and editors to monitor and hold accountable those who exert power in all aspects of public life (watchdog mission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content licensing — Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 3.0 United States License
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, site content is licensed under CC BY-NC 3.0 US: reuse is allowed provided it is noncommercial and the Lab and/or author are attributed, preferably with a link back to the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given of allowed uses under this license: translating the entire site into another language; redistributing posts to students in a course; using the Twitter feed in creative works — provided uses are noncommercial and attribution is given. For other (commercial or unspecified) uses, contact the Lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial emphasis/topics of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab’s coverage emphasizes topics that illustrate how journalism is changing: business models, crowdsourcing, archives and automated context, classifieds reinvention, R&D labs and technology for readers (e-readers, tablets), commenting and community moderation, and examples of newsroom innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page’s recent/featured headlines demonstrate the kinds of stories the Lab prioritizes — case studies, interviews, primers, and analyses that illuminate practices and technologies affecting news organizations and reader engagement.
